# Question: qwen9-data-value

## Recommended gate

Add an **undeclared shortcut-survival gate**: alongside author-declared rivals, run a small repository-owned library of cheap generic structural solvers against each generated lesson. The gate should flag a rival only when it fits every demonstration but predicts a different authoritative answer for the held-out query (and, where practical, its query rotations).

## Reproducible failure it would catch

The pre-repair `d185ceed5cc1` generator always drew full-height left/right borders and one shared internal wall, reducing every row to two fixed chambers. A generic “compact each of two fixed chambers” solver could therefore fit generated demonstrations while failing canonical inputs with row-local walls or open edge segments. The baseline semantic stage was only advisory because no rival contract was declared; a repository-owned rival library would have exposed the shortcut without depending on the generator author to name it.

Useful generic rivals for this task family include ignoring separators, processing only intervals bounded on both sides, sorting values before packing, assuming a fixed separator layout, identity, and whole-row compaction.

## Possible false positive

A generic rival may be extensionally equivalent to the intended rule on the task’s entire lawful domain, or a small finite domain may provide no legal counterexample. It may also survive a short random lesson by chance even though other lawful examples distinguish it. Such a survivor should be reported as “unrefuted on sampled lessons,” not automatically labeled wrong.

## Cheapest test

Materialize 32 fixed-seed lessons per difficulty band with authoritative Racket labels, using the existing lesson-census machinery and roughly 10–20 pure deterministic generic rivals. Cache each rival prediction, rotate the held-out query over already labeled pairs, and fail only on a concrete row where a rival fits all demonstrations and disagrees on the query. Allow a source-bound equivalence waiver when the maintainer demonstrates that the rival is answer-equivalent over the declared lawful domain. This is far cheaper than model inference and directly measures whether the data teaches the intended distinction.
